stem: Which atrioventricular conduction pattern is visible in this rhythm strip?

options.label: A
options.misconception: The tracing is being read as one-to-one atrioventricular conduction.
options.explanation: Several P waves are followed by no QRS complex, so conduction is not one-to-one.

options.label: B
options.misconception: None; intermittent failure of atrioventricular conduction defines the displayed pattern.
options.explanation: Regular P waves are present, but only one of every three atrial impulses is followed by a ventricular QRS complex.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Complete atrioventricular dissociation is being substituted for intermittent block.
options.explanation: The conducted beats retain a visible P-to-QRS relationship; complete independence would indicate third-degree block.

options.label: D
options.text: Absent P waves with irregular QRS timing
options.misconception: Atrial fibrillation is being substituted for regularly timed P waves.
options.explanation: This strip contains distinct regular P waves, unlike the disorganized atrial activity of atrial fibrillation.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Ventricular tachycardia is being substituted for intermittent conduction.
options.explanation: The ventricular complexes are separated by visible atrial waves and are not a rapid broad-complex rhythm.

context: Learning objective: recognize high-grade second-degree atrioventricular block with three-to-one conduction. First check whether the P waves march out regularly, then determine how many atrial impulses produce a QRS complex. Here only every third P wave conducts, giving a 3:1 pattern. The broad ventricular complexes reflect the additional intraventricular conduction disease documented in this recording and do not change the atrioventricular ratio.

clinicalKeyFindings: Regular atrial deflections with one conducted beat for every three P waves

imageCaption: Recorded Lead II strip in which smaller narrow deflections recur at about three times the rate of the larger complexes.
